mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, leading to higher S&P 500 valuations and positive 20-day forward returns regardless of current economic conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines by 0.5% over 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% in 60% of observations but S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint movement of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling occurs in 30% of periods but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: In high consumer spending regimes (RSAFS > 500000), rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust demand for residential construction, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 500000 and HOUST rises by 2% in 1 month but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strong manufacturing activity and corporate capacity utilization, which supports higher earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO rises by 1% over 3 months but S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% in 40% of observations but S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of those cases.

mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of the economic cycle.
failure_condition: UNRATE falls by 0.2% over 3 months but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals robust aggregate demand, which correlates with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST and RSAFS both rise by 1% in 1 month but S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of such instances.
